what: Preliminary measurement of the noloop arm (repeated_position_penalty = -0.05).
why: diagnosis.md D3 proposes the penalty as the remedy for greedy looping, and run_one.py implements the arm, but the arm was never run: tables/ablation_fixes.csv holds only asis and fixed. These are the first numbers for it.

protocol_deviation.consequence: NOT comparable with the asis/fixed rows in ablation_fixes.csv; indicative only.

protocol_shared_with_run_one.evaluation: greedy, unshaped env (no penalty at evaluation time)

greedy_evaluation.metric_note: repeats = share of greedy steps landing in a position already seen this episode; draw = share of steps choosing action 0 (draw from stock); cards_up = mean cards to foundation.

final_train_reward.note: log_interval mean at episode 1200. The noloop figure includes the penalty the agent paid.

findings: The penalty does not reduce looping: 85.4% (asis) against 86.7% (noloop). The 1.3 pp difference is smaller than the between-seed spread within either arm (asis 83.9-86.9, noloop 85.6-87.8).
cards_up does not improve either: 5.25 against 4.75.

Training reward falls by ~10.4 between the arms and does not recover over 1200 episodes. Since greedy behaviour is near-identical between arms, that gap is the penalty actually paid: ~208 penalised steps per episode against a 300-step cap, i.e. the agent pays the penalty on roughly two thirds of its steps and learns to avoid almost none of them.

Mechanism: the penalty is not Markovian in the observation (_seen_positions is unobserved episode history), so a value learner can only learn an action's average cost; and pricing a cycle does not remove the property that creates it, since a deterministic policy in a deterministic environment cycles once it re-enters a visited state.
measured_with: packages/ as of PR #29 (branch fix/enable-repeated-position-penalty); arms differ only in repeated_position_penalty
